title: Lo! What an Entertaining Sight
description: Lo! What an Entertaining Sight in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 918 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christian Union”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lo! what an en-ter-tain-ing sight Those friend-ly bre-thren prove, Whose cheer-ful hearts in bands u-nite Of har-mo-ny and love!

lines: Whose cheerful hearts in bands unite
Where streams of bliss from Christ, the spring,
And heavenly peace, with balmy wing,
Where God his mildest glory shows,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
